text:
luca: Heads-up from zephyrx6b onboarding. After awq int4 (group=64) conversion we see a pronounced collapse in top-k diversity on summarization evals. avg_top5_entropy_fp16=0.52 -> avg_top5_entropy_int4=0.29. Looks head-local.

priya: Did you try with group=128? Some of the earlier converters used 64 for speed and it amplifies head variance.

luca: We tried group=128 and entropy goes to 0.36 (better but not back to 0.52). Command we ran:```bash
python convert.py --in zephyrx6b/fp16 --out zephyrx6b/awq-int4-g64 --quant method=awq,bits=4,group=64 --rotary per_head --export-rot-meta
python eval.py --model zephyrx6b/awq-int4-g64 --task summarization --metrics top5_entropy,ppl
```

ong: The per_head rotary option is suspicious. We recently saw per-head rotary_freq scalars coming out with ~1e-3 jitter which after quant roundtrip can amplify. Can you dump rotary_l2 per head from fp16 vs int4?

luca: Dump attached to s3://redwood-ml/tmp/zephyrx-rot-dumps/rotary_l2_fp16.csv and rotary_l2_int4.csv. Quick glance: several heads show l2_ratio=int4/fp16 ~ 0.67 and a few ~1.4.

maya: Token-level example for prompt "Recent climate policy" — fp16 top5 probs = [0.14,0.09,0.07,0.04,0.03] int4 top5 = [0.42,0.08,0.04,0.02,0.01]. So collapse to top1. Same top1 token, just overconfident.

ong: Repro plan: 1) Run fp16 runtime but apply quantized rotary tables only (simulate converter) 2) Inject gaussian noise scaled to quant step into rotary tables to check sensitivity 3) Try converter using gptq vs awq for rotary projections only.

luca: I ran step 1 this morning. Results: fp16 + quant-rot only -> top5_entropy=0.31 (close to int4), ppl up from 10.1 -> 17.5. So effect isolated to rotary proj.

priya: Sounds like we need a post-quant spectral calibration pass. Idea: compute per-head scaling factor s_h = ||rot_fp16_h||_2 / ||rot_int4_h||_2 and multiply int4 tables by s_h (cheap) before packing. Could be added to convert.py as a flag --rot-calibrate.

ong: Also consider changing grouping for rotary projections only (group=1 or group=head_dim) so they quantize more precisely. Might increase model size slightly but rotary tables are small compared to proj weights.

maya: Small note: check tokenizer grounding too. We saw a similar collapse when vocab merges caused top token to be very frequent; confirm top1 identical between fp16 and int4 (it is). So not a tokenizer OOV.

luca: I prototyped rot-calibrate: after scaling, top5_entropy_int4_cal=0.49, ppl=11.2. Very promising. Pushed prototype to s3://redwood-ml/tmp/zephyrx-rot-calib/ and opened PR draft with patch to convert.py.

priya: Great. If calibration works across models we can upstream to converter. For workflow: 1) add export flag to include raw rot spectral norms in metadata 2) converter can auto-calc s_h and apply prepack 3) add unit test comparing per-head norms between fp16 and post-quant.

stats-bot: eval-job-4932101250 finished: baseline_fp16_ppl=10.1, awq_int4_g64_ppl=17.5, awq_int4_g64_rotcal_ppl=11.2 (attached csv).

ong: Edge case: some models purposefully use per-head scale as a feature (head specialization). Calibration might mask intended differences. We should gate on large deviations (>10%) from mean or only apply when quantization reduces variance beyond threshold.

luca: Agreed. I'll add thresholding logic and a --force-rot-calib flag. Also plan to run a small sweep across a handful of community models (asterion, zephyr, orion variants) before landing.

maya: Please paste minimal repro snippet (load model, replace rot tables, run one prompt) in the PR. Saves time.

luca: Will do. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:
